bullets: Symbolises **greed and its consequences**: each link a selfish act.
‘I made it link by link, and yard by yard; I girded it on of my own free will’: free will and responsibility.
Marley warns that Scrooge’s own chain was as long seven years ago and he has ‘laboured on it since’.
The phantoms outside the window are all chained, wanting to help the poor but unable: regret after death.
Stave 5: Scrooge feels ‘as light as a feather’: freed from his chain.
core.p: Marley’s chain is made of ‘cash-boxes, keys, padlocks, ledgers, deeds, and heavy purses wrought in steel’.

bullets: Stave 1: bells ring before Marley appears: supernatural warning.
Church bells and clock chimes mark the time of each Ghost: time running out.
Stave 5: ‘merry bells’, ‘Clash, clang, hammer; ding, dong, bell. Bell, dong, ding; hammer, clang, clash!’: **onomatopoeia** of celebration and new life.
Cold = Scrooge’s isolation and meanness (‘the cold within him’).
Fire = warmth, family, generosity (Fezziwig, Cratchits, Ghost of Christmas Present).
Stave 5: ‘Make up the fires’: the motif resolved.
**The door knocker** turns into Marley’s face: the supernatural invades Scrooge’s everyday world.
**The extinguisher cap**: Scrooge tries to suppress memory/truth.
**Tiny Tim’s crutch**: his vulnerability; in Stave 4 it is ‘carefully preserved’ without an owner.
**The grave**: neglected, overgrown: the end of a life without love.
**The bed curtains**: stolen in Stave 4; in Stave 5 Scrooge clutches them joyfully: ‘They are not torn down’.

callouts.p: Dickens’s symbols make abstract ideas physical: chains make greed visible, bells make time audible, and fire and cold make generosity and isolation something the reader can feel.

model: Context: Christian ideas of sin and judgement
exam.q: Explain the importance of symbolism in the novella. (20 marks)
exam.tip: Choose 3–4 symbols and track each across the staves.

mistakes.r: Explain what each one represents and how it develops.

Clash, clang, hammer; ding, dong, bell

quotes.a: Relief: the future can be changed.

summary: Key symbols and motifs (Marley’s chains, bells, cold and fire, and others such as the door knocker, Tiny Tim’s crutch and the extinguisher cap) carry Dickens’s ideas about greed, time, isolation and redemption.
